description.narrative:
The proposed project will advance gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls and contribute to SDG target 5.4 (“recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work through the provision of public services, infrastructure and social protection policies and the promotion of shared responsibility within the household and the family as nationally appropriate”).
The expected outcome of the project is for governments in seven target countries across the Arab States, Asia and the Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean to gain new capacities for the design and implementation of care policies that recognize, reduce and redistribute unpaid care work, while rewarding and representing paid care work. The target countries identified are Algeria, Chile, Colombia, Lao PDR, Mexico, Syrian Arab Republic and Timor-Leste. In Lao PDR specifically, the expected outcome of the project is to contribute to building the country’s national care system and bridging the economic gap between women and men. This outcome is expected to be achieved through the generation and transfer of knowledge as well as through technical assistance to target ministries responsible for addressing the care economy, building their capacities to develop national action plans and strategies that build a comprehensive care system.
As the COVID-19 pandemic unfolded, ESCAP worked with member States and the ASEAN Committee on Women (ACW), to take stock of the situation and address the impacts of the unpaid care and domestic work on women and girls. This work, including a regional report on thetopic (September 2021) has already been held in high regard by the ACW and a joint report including policy guidelines on this topicwas recently launched in the margins of the 4th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Women (in October 2021). Building on the regional and subregional analytical work, the project will carry out further national studies, which form the evidence base for convening multi-stakeholder consultations, as well as developing and instituting policy initiatives to recognize, reduce and redistribute unpaid careand domestic work, including scaling up national investment in care infrastructure, care services and gender responsive social protection measures necessary to realize the full potential of women and girls. A policy toolkit comprising model frameworks for action on the care economy has been developed which will assist governments, with good practices promoted among Asia-Pacific countries through the ESCAP regional platform.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
